subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What recurring types of problems show up in these incident tickets?

judge.implied_focus: The nature/type of the underlying problem in each incident ticket (categorizing recurring problem types by category, affected component, and failure symptom)

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Directly captures the type of problem (email, database, vpn), the core axis for identifying recurring problem types.

per_column.name: affected_system_component
per_column.rationale: Adds a finer-grained facet of the problem (which specific component fails), differentiating within categories.

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: Captures the manifestation of the problem (cannot_connect, access_denied), a coherent third facet enabling problem-type clustering.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Constant 'true' for all 500 rows -- zero variance, no analytical value; a vacuous restatement of the query rather than a real signal.

per_column.name: ticket_resolved
per_column.rationale: Resolution status is a lifecycle/outcome attribute, not part of characterizing the problem type; peripheral to the focus.

per_column.name: assignment_status
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket is assigned is a workflow attribute unrelated to identifying recurring problem types.

judge.rationale: The first three columns (category, component, symptom) form a genuinely coherent, well-structured decomposition of 'problem type' at a useful granularity, enabling an analyst to cluster and rank recurring problem patterns -- clearly actionable. However, coherence is diluted by a grab-bag of three off-focus columns: recurrence_signal is a degenerate constant (true for all 500) adding no information, while ticket_resolved and assignment_status are workflow/lifecycle attributes rather than problem-characterizing facets. The strong core keeps the implied focus recognizable and inferable, but the extraneous columns prevent this from being a tight, single-focus structure.
